story_type: heat shield warning on the first American orbital flight, 1962 mission film
hook: A signal said his heat shield had come loose.
narration: Up in orbit, a signal said his heat shield had come loose.
February 20th, 1962. John Glenn was flying Friendship 7.
First, a fault in the automatic control system made the capsule yaw, so Glenn flew it by hand.
Then ground stations picked up a chilling signal. The heat shield seemed to have come loose.
Could the signal be wrong? There was no way to tell.
If it was true, he could die in the three thousand degree heat of reentry.
The retro rockets were strapped over the shield. Left on after firing, their straps might hold it in place.
[short pause] As he plunged back in, the heat of reentry cut off all voice contact.
outcome: Friendship 7 came through, and after four hours and fifty six minutes the destroyer Noa picked up John Glenn.
title: Heat shield warning on Friendship 7
description:
On Feb. 20, 1962, during the first American orbital flight, ground stations received a signal that John Glenn's heat shield on Friendship 7 had come loose. Glenn came through reentry and was recovered by the destroyer Noa. From the 1962 NASA film Friendship 7.
